_strings.@@08572705cd78: Illinois Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — In general, anyone who qualified for the federal EITC also qualifies for the Illinois EITC. For tax year 2023 and after, eligibility is expanded beyond the federal qualifications: taxpayers who meet all federal EITC qualifications EXCEPT that they file with an IRS-issued ITIN (no valid SSN required for taxpayer, spouse, or qualifying children), and/or are age 18-24 or 65+ with no qualifying child, may also claim it. Must have earned income under the federal limits in Table 1, investment income below $11,600, not have filed federal Form 2555, and meet the other federal EITC rules.

_strings.@@15c7d4d5ec55: Illinois Property Tax Credit — Illinois residents who paid Illinois property tax in 2024 on their principal residence (not a vacation home or rental property) for the time they owned and lived at the property during 2023, where that residence was in Illinois. Not available for mobile home privilege tax, penalties/fees, property outside Illinois, or the portion of property tax deductible as a business expense. Nonresidents may not take this credit.

_strings.@@5672d6b345b7: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit EXPANDED for 2024 by Public Act 103-0592 to include volunteers registered with the Illinois Emergency Management Agency (IEMA) and Office of Homeland Security (OHS) who volunteered at least 100 hours during the immediately preceding calendar year, in addition to the previously covered non-full-time fire department / fire protection district / fire protection association volunteers. The credit remains $500 per awarded individual ($1,000 if married filing jointly and both spouses were awarded), certificate-based, capped statewide at $5,000,000 and at the first 10,000 qualified applicants. Resolve via: 2024 Schedule ICR Section C (Lines 10-11) and its instructions (R-12/24) — requires a 2024 Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit Certificate issued by IDOR; the nonrefundable total on Schedule ICR Line 13 is carried to Form IL-1040 Line 16 and cannot exceed tax due.

_strings.@@7102c86cc868: K-12 Education Expense Credit — Parent or legal guardian of a full-time student who was under age 21 at the close of the school year, where the taxpayer and student were Illinois residents when the expenses were paid, and the student attended kindergarten through 12th grade at a public or nonpublic school in Illinois during 2024. Must complete Section B of Schedule ICR including the K-12 Education Expense Credit Worksheet and keep school receipts.
_strings.@@7e241fba96f3: Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit — Available only to a person who received a 2024 Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit Certificate from IDOR. Expanded for 2024 by Public Act 103-0592 to include volunteers registered with the Illinois Emergency Management Agency (IEMA) and Office of Homeland Security (OHS) who volunteered at least 100 hours during the immediately preceding calendar year, in addition to non-full-time fire department/fire protection district/fire protection association volunteers. Must have served as a volunteer emergency worker at least 9 months during the taxable year, not receive more than $5,000 in compensation for those services, apply with IDOR, and be one of the first 10,000 qualified applicants. Note: the income limit that applies to the property tax / K-12 credits does NOT apply to this credit.

_strings.@@ea4747dd0151: Treaty conformity — IL conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IL income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IL return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: IL-1040 starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2024 IL-1040 Step 2, Line 1 "Adjusted gross income — Enter the adjusted gross income from your federal return." The instructions ("What is Illinois income?") confirm "Your Illinois income includes the adjusted gross income (AGI) amount figured on your federal return, plus any additional income that must be added to your AGI." Income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI, so it flows through and is not re-taxed. Illinois additions are limited: Line 2 "Federally tax-exempt income" applies ONLY to federally tax-exempt interest and dividend income reported on federal Form 1040 Line 2a (municipal bond interest), not to foreign treaty income; Line 3/Schedule M "Other additions" enumerates specific items (child's 8814 interest/dividends, pass-through additions, Section 529/ABLE earnings, IL-4562 special depreciation, business expense recapture, etc.) and contains no add-back of federal income-tax-treaty-exempt income. There is NO California-style Schedule CA treaty addback. Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed and IL conforms.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@f568534dd771: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW Illinois Child Tax Credit for tax year 2024 (Public Act 103-0592), added on Form IL-1040 Line 30: available to taxpayers who qualify for the Illinois EITC and have at least one dependent child under the age of 12 as of the last day of 2024, calculated as 20% of the taxpayer's Illinois EITC (2024 Schedule IL-E/EITC Step 5, Line 12 'Multiply the amount on Line 11 by 20% (0.2). This is your Illinois Child Tax Credit'). Refundable — the schedule notes the total Illinois EITC and Child Tax Credit may exceed the amount of tax. Resolve via: 2024 Schedule IL-E/EITC Step 5 (Lines 11-12) — 20% of the Illinois EITC computed in Step 4 — carried to Form IL-1040 Line 30. calc.state_tax computes only the Line 12 tax, so the credit is applied after it in Step 8 (Payments and Refundable Credit).

This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Dependent exemptions (Line 10d) ship for 2024: the 2024 Schedule IL-E/EITC form prints the per-dependent multiplication (Step 2 Line 1, $2,775 per dependent), so dependents_count is applied at $2,775 each. Attach Schedule IL-E/EITC when claiming dependents. Exemption phase-out: the entire Line 10 exemption allowance (including Lines 10b-10d) is $0 when federal AGI exceeds $500,000 (married filing jointly) or $250,000 (all other statuses) — the 'Income Exceptions' box in the Line 10 instructions. Claimed as a dependent by another: if base income exceeds $2,775, the filer's own exemption is $0 (Line 10a chart rows with the Step 1 Line C box checked).
